title: Exterior sheaf map induced by a module morphism
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $M,N$ sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, $f:M\to N$ a morphism, and $n\in\mathbb N$. For the exterior sheaves and wedge sections [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], there exists $e:\bigwedge^n M\to\bigwedge^n N$ such that for every open $U$ and tuple $a\in M(U)^n$, $e_U(\bigwedge_i a_i)=\bigwedge_i f_U(a_i)$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: exterior-power universal properties and independence of quotient lifts

proof.text: On each open define the map by exteriorPower.map applied to the component of f. Its value on a pure wedge is the wedge of the component images.

Check naturality on pure wedges. The unique exterior restrictions take a wedge to the wedge of the restrictions, and naturality of f identifies the two resulting tuples. Pure wedges span, so exteriorPower.linearMap_ext gives the naturality equality.
Apply the sheafification functor to this explicit presheaf morphism. Naturality of its adjunction unit, evaluated on the pure wedge, gives the asserted formula.

lean.statement:
theorem exteriorSheaf_map_exists {X : Scheme.{v}} {M N : X.Modules}
    (f : M ⟶ N) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : exteriorPower M n ⟶ exteriorPower N n,
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (a : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)),
        e.val.app (op U) (wedge (M := M) (r := n) (U := U) a) =
          wedge (M := N) (r := n) (U := U) (fun i ↦ f.val.app (op U) (a i))
lean.note: Retired the Sheaf copy in favor of the upstream exteriorPower/wedge theorem. The remaining Sheaf consumer identifies its exteriorSheafPresheaf with the upstream presheaf by the identity on section modules, using uniqueness of exterior restrictions, and sheafifies this explicit isomorphism. Naturality of the unit proves that both directions preserve wedge sections.
